text.paragraph: Establishing primary care for chronic C2 tetraplegia on a ventilator, some weeks after a diaphragm pacing system was implanted: autonomic dysreflexia plan, skin, bladder, bowel, respiratory care, bone and cardiometabolic health, mood, and care team needs. Concerns: He wants to spend longer each day breathing with the pacer instead of the ventilator; He wants to keep working and traveling without a hospital stay, and to keep his skin healthy; He wants to keep building strength and sensation through his exercise program. [S]

tr.td: Sennosides 8.6 mg oral tablet, two tablets at bedtime

Nitroglycerin 2% ointment, one inch to the skin of the chest only if systolic blood pressure stays at 150 mmHg or higher after the first steps of the autonomic dysreflexia plan; wipe off when pressure falls
As needed for autonomic dysreflexia, under the written plan
Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, two tablets up to three times a day as needed for neck and shoulder aching
Two tablets up to three times a day as needed

Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) of the hip, with distal femur and proximal tibia views
Ultrasound of both kidneys and the bladder
Advance care planning conversation, about 30 minutes

text.paragraph: Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

tr.td: Fractures of the first and second cervical vertebrae with spinal cord injury in a riding fall; unable to breathe on his own afterwards

Activity-based recovery program (electrically stimulated cycling and pool therapy) begun about five years after the injury; by his physicians' report, improvement from ASIA grade A to C, reversal of osteoporosis, less spasticity, and far fewer infections
Diaphragm pacing system implanted laparoscopically in Cleveland; able to breathe more than two hours off the ventilator afterwards

tr.td: Establishing primary care for chronic C2 tetraplegia on a ventilator, some weeks after a diaphragm pacing system was implanted: autonomic dysreflexia plan, skin, bladder, bowel, respiratory care, bone and cardiometabolic health, mood, and care team needs
Two-week review and physical medicine and rehabilitation (spinal cord injury medicine) consultation, with a bone density scan and kidney and bladder ultrasound
Ten-week review: pacer conditioning, skin, vitamin D, and seating
Four-month review: kidney function, skin, mood, and equipment
Six-month review: respiratory care, skin, bladder and kidney surveillance, vaccines, and plans for the winter

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Autonomic dysreflexia: a written plan and wallet card (sit him up, loosen clothing, check the catheter and bladder, then the bowel and skin; check blood pressure every 2 to 5 minutes; nitroglycerin ointment only if systolic pressure stays at 150 mmHg or higher), his baseline blood pressure recorded, and training for every nurse

Physical medicine and rehabilitation (spinal cord injury medicine) consultation to review the pacer conditioning plan, the autonomic dysreflexia plan, bladder and bowel management, bone health, spasticity and pain, and seating and equipment

Pressure injury prevention: skin checks morning and night by his nurses, tilt-in-space pressure relief every 30 minutes in the chair, turning every 2 hours in bed on a pressure-redistributing mattress, cushion and seating review, nutrition, and the Braden scale at each visit

Neurogenic bladder: catheter care with monthly changes and closed drainage, no treatment of bacteria in the urine without symptoms, kidney function by cystatin C, and kidney and bladder ultrasound yearly
Neurogenic bowel: a daily morning program with a suppository and digital stimulation, senna at night, fiber and fluids, reviewed at each visit

Respiratory care: tracheostomy care, suctioning, daily mechanical insufflation-exsufflation for secretion clearance, a pacer conditioning schedule with oxygen saturation checks, a backup ventilator, a spare tracheostomy tube, a generator and battery plan for power cuts, and registration with the power company and emergency services

Bone health and cardiometabolic risk: calcium, 25-hydroxyvitamin D and PTH, DXA of the hip and knee regions, continued electrically stimulated cycling, careful transfers; lipids, A1c and blood pressure yearly

Mood, pain, spasticity and venous thromboembolism: PHQ-9 at intake and twice a year, pain score at reviews, stretching and range of motion for spasticity, and checking for leg swelling, with urgent assessment for a new swollen leg

On the consultant's advice: vitamin D3 1977 units daily with a recheck in about eight weeks, seating pressure mapping with a cushion review, a weekly step-up of pacer time as tolerated, and a repeat DXA in two years
Lengthen time on the diaphragm pacer to at least three hours twice a day by six months, with stable oxygen saturation
Pacer three hours twice a day; saturation 97 to 98% on the pacer
No pressure injury: skin intact at every check through six months
Skin intact at every visit; Braden 11 to 12
Written autonomic dysreflexia plan held by him and every nurse, with all nurses trained, by the two-week visit
Plan and wallet card in place; all regular nurses trained
25-hydroxyvitamin D at least 30 ng/mL within three months
No unplanned hospital admission through six months

list.item: Drives a power wheelchair with tilt-in-space himself; needs full assistance for transfers, bathing, dressing, bladder and bowel care; sits up for most of the day; speaks with the tracheostomy cuff deflated; some voluntary finger and wrist movement and sensation over much of his body [S]
Alert, articulate and engaged; mood good; future-oriented and focused on his work and his recovery goals; PHQ-9 score 3 [S]
